title: U.S. House · Illinois's 9th District
area: Chicago's North Side and North Shore suburbs, including Evanston, Skokie, Rogers Park and Glenview.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Jan Schakowsky did not run for re-election. Daniel K. Biss, the mayor of Evanston, won a crowded March 17, 2026 Democratic primary with 29.4% of the vote over Kat Abughazaleh (26.3%), Laura Fine (20.0%) and twelve other candidates. John Elleson won the Republican primary. Ballotpedia calculated the district's Cook Partisan Voter Index as D+19, based on the 2020 and 2024 presidential elections.

candidates.name: Daniel K. Biss
candidates.currentRole: Mayor of Evanston (since 2021; announced he would resign Oct. 18, 2026)

summary.text: Daniel Biss is the Democratic nominee for the open Illinois 9th District seat. A mathematician by training, he served in the Illinois House and Senate, finished second in the 2018 Democratic primary for governor, and was elected mayor of Evanston in 2021 and re-elected in 2025. He won the crowded March 2026 Democratic primary; according to his campaign website, he is running on rebuilding an economy that works for everyone and limiting corporate consolidation.

background.text: Born August 27, 1977, in Akron, Ohio, to a family of professional musicians, and attended Bloomington North High School in Bloomington, Indiana.
Earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from Harvard University in 1998 and a Ph.D. in mathematics from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 2002.
Was an assistant professor of mathematics at the University of Chicago from 2002 to 2008, and a Clay Research Fellow from 2002 to 2007.
Lost a 2008 bid for the Illinois House 17th District, then worked as a policy adviser to Gov. Pat Quinn beginning in 2009.
Served in the Illinois House of Representatives from 2011 to 2013 and in the Illinois Senate (9th District) from 2013 to 2019.
Chaired the Illinois Senate Human Services Committee in the 2015 session and the Labor Committee in the 2017 session.
Ended a 2015 campaign for state comptroller and endorsed Susana Mendoza. In 2018 he ran for governor and finished second in the Democratic primary with 26.7% to JB Pritzker's 45.1%.

After leaving the Senate, became executive director of the nonprofit Rust Belt Rising, which aims to train and support Democratic candidates in Great Lakes states, and worked as a clean energy consultant.

Took office as mayor of Evanston on May 10, 2021, and was re-elected April 1, 2025, with 62.7% of the vote. In June 2026 he announced he would resign on October 18 to trigger a spring special election; this guide did not find confirmation that the resignation has taken effect.
Announced his congressional candidacy in May 2025 for the seat of retiring Rep. Jan Schakowsky, who endorsed him in January 2026, and won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary with 29.4% of the vote.

summary.text: John Elleson is the Republican nominee for Illinois's 9th District, a pastor who also ran for the seat in 2018 and lost to Rep. Jan Schakowsky. He won the March 2026 Republican primary and describes himself as a compassionate conservative; his Ballotpedia survey cites addiction, homelessness, mental health, healthcare and job creation as priorities.

background.text: Born in Monmouth, Illinois, and graduated from Christian Life College. BallotReady lists a bachelor's degree in theology from the college in 1985.

Works as a pastor; BallotReady lists him as pastor of Lakewood Chapel since 1985 and also lists experience as a donut shop owner and baker. His Ballotpedia profile and 2018 survey list no prior elected office.
Ran as the Republican nominee for the 9th District in 2018 and lost to Jan Schakowsky, 73.5% to 26.5%.
Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary with 48.9% of the vote, ahead of Paul Friedman (33.6%), Rocio Cleveland and Mark Su.
Describes himself as having decades of service in the community and a proven track record of integrity and results.
background.quote: I'm a compassionate conservative with common sense, and I bring a steady, unifying voice to a divided political climate.

priorities.text: Says he supports practical, aid-based programs for addiction, homelessness and mental health, and community-first healthcare policies expanding local clinics.
Says he would support law enforcement with resources and de-escalation training while focusing on keeping drugs off the streets.
Says he supports policies that uplift working families while protecting religious liberty, and removing burdensome business regulations.

positions.summary: Says he supports resourcing and training law enforcement, focused on de-escalation and community trust.
Says he supports community-first healthcare policies and expanding local clinics without federal overreach.

researchNotes: Biss has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his key messages are drawn from a campaign advertisement and campaign website as summarized by Ballotpedia staff. Biography gaps: Elleson's pastorate and degree year come from BallotReady, and no campaign site or news profile of his 2026 run was found; Biss's mayoral resignation (announced for Oct. 18, 2026) was reported by local media but not confirmed as completed.
